verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part 1 - Samādhi-pāda - Yoga and its Aims</vt>
अथ योगानुशासनम् ॥ १.१॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part 1 - Samādhi-pāda - Yoga and its Aims</vt>
atha yogānuśāsanam .. 1.1..
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part 1 - Samādhi-pāda - Yoga and its Aims</vt>
atha yoganushasanam .. 1.1..
yogah chitta vritti nirodhah .. .2..
verses.translation_reworded: Yoga is holding the mind-stuff (Chitta) back from assuming different forms (Vrittis).

verses.colloquial: tadaa drashtuh svaruupe'vasthaanam .. .3..
verses.translation_reworded: Then (once all the waves have ended; this has nothing to do with concentration) the seer (Purusha) abides in his own (unmodified) state.

verses.colloquial: vritti saaruupyam itaratra .. .4..
verses.translation_reworded: At other times (apart from concentration) the seer is identified with the modifications.

verses.colloquial: vrittayah panchatayyah klishtaa 'aklishtaah .. .5..
verses.translation_reworded: The modifications fall into five classes, (some) painful and (others) not.

verses.colloquial: pramaana viparyaya vikalpa nidraa smritayah .. .6..
verses.translation_reworded: (They are) right knowledge, indiscrimination, verbal delusion, sleep, and memory.

verses.colloquial: pratyaksha anumaana aagamaah pramaanaani .. .7..
verses.translation_reworded: The proofs are direct perception, inference, and competent evidence.

verses.colloquial: viparyayah mithyaa jnaanam atadruupa pratishtham .. .8..
verses.translation_reworded: Indiscrimination is false knowledge, not grounded in the real nature of a thing.

verses.colloquial: shabda jnaana anupaatii vastu shuunyah vikalpah .. .9..
verses.translation_reworded: Verbal delusion arises from words with no (corresponding) reality.

verses.colloquial: abhaava pratyaya aalambanaa vrittir nidraa .. .10..
verses.translation_reworded: Sleep is a Vritti that holds the feeling of voidness.

verses.colloquial: anubhuuta vishaya asampramoshah smritih .. .11..
verses.translation_reworded: Memory occurs when the (Vrittis of) perceived subjects do not slip away (and return to consciousness through impressions).

verses.colloquial: abhyaasa vairaagyaabhyaam tan nirodhah .. .12..
verses.translation_reworded: They are controlled through practice and non-attachment.

verses.colloquial: tatra sthitau yatnah abhyaasah .. .13..
verses.translation_reworded: Practice is the continuous struggle to hold them (the Vrittis) fully in check.

verses.colloquial: sa tu diirgha kaala nairantarya satkaara aasevito dridha bhuumih .. .14..
verses.translation_reworded: Long, unbroken effort with great love (for the goal) makes it firmly rooted.

verses.colloquial: drishta anushravika vishaya vitrishnasya vashiikaara samjnaa vairaagyam .. .15..
verses.translation_reworded: Non-attachment is the state that comes to those who have dropped their thirst for objects, seen or heard of, and that wills to control those objects.

verses.colloquial: tatparam purusha khyaater guna vaitrishnyam .. .16..
verses.translation_reworded: Extreme non-attachment gives up even the qualities and arises from knowledge of (the real nature of) the Purusha.

verses.colloquial: vitarka vichaara aananda asmitaa ruupa anugamaat samprajnaatah .. .17..
verses.translation_reworded: The concentration called right knowledge is accompanied by reasoning, discrimination, bliss, and unqualified egoism.

verses.colloquial: viraama pratyaya abhyaasa puurvah samskaara shesho'nyah .. .18..
verses.translation_reworded: Another Samadhi comes through constant practice of stopping all mental activity; in it the Chitta holds only unmanifested impressions.

verses.colloquial: bhava pratyayo videha prakriti layaanaam .. .19..
verses.translation_reworded: (Without extreme non-attachment, this Samadhi) causes the re-manifestation of the gods and of those merged in nature.

verses.colloquial: shraddhaa viirya smriti samaadhi prajnaa puurvaka itareshaam .. .20..
verses.translation_reworded: For others, (this Samadhi) comes through faith, energy, memory, concentration, and discrimination of the real.

verses.colloquial: tiivra samvegaanaam aasannah .. .21..
verses.translation_reworded: The intensely energetic succeed quickly.

verses.colloquial: mridu madhya adhi maatratvaat tato'pi visheshah .. .22..
verses.translation_reworded: Yogis' success varies with whether their means are mild, medium, or intense.

verses.colloquial: iishvara pranidhaanaad vaa .. .23..
verses.translation_reworded: Or through devotion to Ishvara.

verses.colloquial: klesha karma vipaaka aashayair aparaamrishtah purusha vishesha iishvarah .. .24..
verses.translation_reworded: A particular Purusha, free from misery, karma, its fruits and desire, is Ishvara (the Supreme Ruler).

verses.colloquial: tatra niratishayam saarva jnabiijam .. .25..
verses.translation_reworded: In Him, the all-knowingness that is (only) a germ in others becomes infinite.

verses.colloquial: sa puurveshaam api guruh kaalena anavacchedaat .. .26..
verses.translation_reworded: Not limited by time, He is the Teacher even of the ancient teachers.

verses.colloquial: tasya vaachakah pranavah .. .27..
verses.translation_reworded: Om is the word that manifests Him.

verses.colloquial: tajjapah tadartha bhaavanam .. .28..
verses.translation_reworded: Repeating this (Om) and meditating on its meaning (is the way).

verses.colloquial: tatah pratyak chetana adhigamah api antaraaya abhaavah cha .. .29..
verses.translation_reworded: This brings (knowledge of) introspection and destroys obstacles.

verses.colloquial:
vyaadhi styaana samshaya pramaada aalasya avirati-
bhraanti darshana alabdha bhuumikatva anavasthitatvaani
chitta vikshepaas te 'ntaraayaah .. .30..
verses.translation_reworded: The distractions that obstruct are disease, mental laziness, doubt, lack of enthusiasm, lethargy, clinging to sense-enjoyments, false perception, failure to reach concentration, and slipping from that state once reached.

verses.colloquial: duhkha daurmanasya anga mejayatva shvaasa prashvaasaa vikshepa sahabhuvah .. .31..
verses.translation_reworded: Grief, mental distress, trembling of the body, and irregular breathing come with the failure to hold concentration.

verses.colloquial: tatpratishedha artham ekatattva abhyaasah .. .32..
verses.translation_reworded: As a remedy, (one should) practise on one subject.

verses.colloquial:
maitrii karunaa mudita upekshaanaam sukha duhkha punya apunya vishayaanaam
bhaavanaatah chitta prasaadanam .. .33..
verses.translation_reworded: Thinking with friendship, mercy, gladness, and indifference toward subjects that are happy, unhappy, good, and evil, respectively, calms the Chitta.

verses.colloquial: pracchardana vidhaaranaabhyaam vaa praanasya .. .34..
verses.translation_reworded: By expelling and holding the Breath.

verses.colloquial: vishayavatii vaa pravrittih utpannaa manasah sthiti nibandhinii .. .35..
verses.translation_reworded: Forms of concentration that bring extraordinary sense-perceptions make the mind persevere.

verses.colloquial: vishokaa vaa jyotishmatii .. .36..
verses.translation_reworded: Or (by meditating on) the Effulgent Light, beyond all sorrow.

verses.colloquial: viita raaga vishayam vaa chittam .. .37..
verses.translation_reworded: Or (by meditating on) the heart that has dropped all attachment to sense-objects.

verses.colloquial: svapna nidraa jnaana aalambanam vaa .. .38..
verses.translation_reworded: Knowledge arising in sleep, taken as an object of meditation, also serves.

verses.colloquial: yathaabhimata dhyaanaad vaa .. .39..
verses.translation_reworded: Or by meditating on anything one finds good.

verses.colloquial: paramaanu parama mahattvaantah asya vashiikaarah .. .40..
verses.translation_reworded: Meditating in this way, the Yogi's mind becomes unobstructed, from the atomic to the infinite.

verses.colloquial:
kshiina vritteh abhijaatasya iva maneh grahiitri grahana graahyeshu
tatstha tadanjanataa samaapattih .. .41..
verses.translation_reworded: The Yogi whose Vrittis have thus lost their power (are controlled) gains concentratedness and sameness in the receiver, (the instrument of) receiving, and the received (the Self, the mind, and external objects), like a crystal (before objects of different colours).

verses.colloquial: tatra shabda artha jnaana vikalpaih samkiirnaa savitarkaa samaapattih .. .42..
verses.translation_reworded: When sound, meaning, and resulting knowledge are mixed together, it is (called) Samadhi with question.

verses.colloquial: smriti parishuddhau svaruupa shuunyeva artha maatra nirbhaasaa nirvitarkaa .. .43..
verses.translation_reworded: The Samadhi called "without question" (comes) when memory is purified, or free of qualities, and expresses only the meaning (of the object meditated on).

verses.sanskrit: एतयैव सविचारा निर्विचारा च सूक्ष्मविषया व्याख्याता ॥ १.४४॥
verses.roman: etayaiva savicārā nirvicārā ca sūkṣmaviṣayā vyākhyātā .. 1.44..
verses.colloquial: etayaa eva savichaaraa nirvichaaraa cha suukshma vishayaa vyaakhyaataa .. .44..
verses.translation_reworded: This process also explains (the concentrations) with and without discrimination, whose objects are finer.

verses.colloquial: suukshma vishayatvam cha alinga paryavasaanam .. .45..
verses.translation_reworded: Pradhāna is the limit of the finer objects.

verses.colloquial: taa eva sabiijah samaadhih .. .46..
verses.translation_reworded: These concentrations have seed.

verses.colloquial: nirvichaara vaishaaradye'dhyaatma prasaadah .. .47..
verses.translation_reworded: When the concentration "without discrimination" is purified, the Chitta becomes firmly fixed.

verses.colloquial: ritambharaa tatra prajnaa .. .48..
verses.translation_reworded: The knowledge in that state is called "filled with Truth."

verses.colloquial: shruta anumaana prajnaabhyaam anya vishayaa vishesha arthatvaat .. .49..
verses.translation_reworded: Knowledge from testimony and inference concerns common objects. Knowledge from the Samadhi just mentioned is far higher, reaching where inference and testimony cannot go.

verses.colloquial: tajjah samskaarah anya samskaara pratibandhii .. .50..
verses.translation_reworded: The impression left by this Samadhi blocks all other impressions.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यापि निरोधे सर्वनिरोधान्निर्बीजः समाधिः ॥ १.५१॥
॥ इति पतञ्जलि-विरचिते योग-सूत्रे प्रथमः समाधि-पादः ॥
verses.roman:
tasyāpi nirodhe sarvanirodhānnirbījaḥ samādhiḥ .. 1.51..
.. iti patañjali-viracite yoga-sūtre prathamaḥ samādhi-pādaḥ ..
verses.colloquial:
tasyaapi nirodhe sarva nirodhaan nirbiijah samaadhih ..
.. iti patanjali-virachite yoga-suutre prathamah samaadhi-paadah ..
verses.translation_reworded: When even this (impression, which blocks all others) is restrained, everything is restrained, and the "seedless" Samadhi comes.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part 2 - Sādhana-pāda - Yoga and its Practice</vt>
तपःस्वाध्यायेश्वरप्रणिधानानि क्रियायोगः ॥ २.१॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part 2 - Sādhana-pāda - Yoga and its Practice</vt>
tapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni kriyāyogaḥ .. 2.1..
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part  - Saadhana-paada - Yoga and its Practiche</vt>
tapah svaadhyaaya iishvara pranidhaanaani kriyaa yogah .. .1..
verses.translation_reworded: Kriyā-Yoga consists of mortification, study, and offering the results of one's work to God.

verses.colloquial: samaadhi bhaavana arthah klesha tanuukarana arthash cha .. .2..
verses.translation_reworded: (It serves) the practice of Samadhi and the reduction of the pain-bearing obstructions.

verses.colloquial: avidyaa asmitaa raaga dvesha abhiniveshaah kleshaah .. .3..
verses.translation_reworded: Ignorance, egoism, attachment, aversion and clinging to life: these are the obstructions that bring pain.

verses.colloquial: avidyaa kshetram uttareshaam prasupta tanu vicchinna udaaraanaam .. .4..
verses.translation_reworded: Ignorance is the field in which all the others grow, whether dormant, weakened, overpowered, or expanded.

verses.colloquial: anitya ashuchi duhkha anaatmasu nitya shuchi sukha aatma khyaatih avidyaa .. .5..
verses.translation_reworded: Ignorance mistakes the non-eternal, impure, painful, and non-Self for the eternal, pure, happy, and the Atman or Self (respectively).

verses.colloquial: drig darshana shaktyoh ekaatmataa iva asmitaa .. .6..
verses.translation_reworded: Egoism is identifying the seer with the instrument of seeing.

verses.colloquial: sukha anushayii raagah .. .7..
verses.translation_reworded: Attachment is what dwells on pleasure.

verses.colloquial: duhkha anushayii dveshah .. .8..
verses.translation_reworded: Aversion is what dwells on pain.

verses.colloquial: svarasa vaahii vidusho'pi tathaa ruudho'bhiniveshah .. .9..
verses.translation_reworded: Clinging to life flows by its own nature and is established even in the learned.

verses.colloquial: te prati prasava heyaah suukshmaah .. .10..
verses.translation_reworded: The fine Samskaras are overcome by resolving them into their causal state.

verses.colloquial: dhyaana heyaah tad vrittayah .. .11..
verses.translation_reworded: Their gross modifications are to be cast off through meditation.

verses.colloquial: klesha muulah karma aashayah drishta adrishta janma vedaniiyah .. .12..
verses.translation_reworded: These pain-bearing obstructions are the root of the "receptacle of works," which is experienced in this visible life or in the unseen life.

verses.colloquial: sati muule tad vipaako jaati aayur bhogaah .. .13..
verses.translation_reworded: While the root remains, it ripens as species, life, and the experience of pleasure and pain.

verses.colloquial: te hlaada paritaapa phalaah punya apunya hetutvaat .. .14..
verses.translation_reworded: Virtue yields them as pleasure; vice yields them as pain.

verses.colloquial:
parinaama taapa samskaara duhkhair guna vritti virodhaac cha
duhkham eva sarvam vivekinah .. .15..
verses.translation_reworded: For the discriminating, everything is painful, as it were. All things bring pain as a consequence, as anticipated loss of happiness, as new craving born of impressions of happiness, and as the counteraction of qualities.

verses.colloquial: heyam duhkham anaagatam .. .16..
verses.translation_reworded: Misery yet to come is to be avoided.

verses.colloquial: drashtri drishyayoh samyogo heya hetuh .. .17..
verses.translation_reworded: What is to be avoided is caused by the junction of seer and seen.

verses.colloquial:
prakaasha kriyaa sthiti shiilam bhuuta indriya aatmakam
bhoga apavarga artham drishyam .. .18..
verses.translation_reworded: The experienced consists of elements and organs. Its nature is illumination, action and inertia, and it exists for the experience and release of the experiencer.

verses.colloquial: vishesha avishesha linga maatra alingaani guna parvaani .. .19..
verses.translation_reworded: The qualities have four states: defined, undefined, indicated only, and signless.

verses.colloquial: drashtaa drishimaatrah shuddho'pi pratyayaanupashyah .. .20..
verses.translation_reworded: The seer is intelligence alone. Though pure, it sees by way of the colouring of the intellect.

verses.colloquial: tad artha eva drishyasya aatmaa .. .21..
verses.translation_reworded: The experienced exists, by its nature, for him.

verses.colloquial: kritaartham prati nashtam api anashtam tad anya saadhaaranatvaat .. .22..
verses.translation_reworded: For one who has reached the goal it is destroyed; yet it is not destroyed, being shared with others.

verses.colloquial: sva svaami shaktyoh svaruupa upalabdhi hetuh samyogah .. .23..
verses.translation_reworded: Junction brings about realisation of the nature of both powers, the experienced and its Lord.

verses.colloquial: tasya hetur avidyaa .. .24..
verses.translation_reworded: Its cause is ignorance.

verses.colloquial: tad abhaavaat samyoga abhaavo haanam taddrisheh kaivalyam .. .25..
verses.translation_reworded: Without ignorance there is no junction, the thing to be avoided. That is the independence of the seer.

verses.colloquial: viveka khyaatih aviplavaa haana upaayah .. .26..
verses.translation_reworded: Ignorance is destroyed by unbroken practice of discrimination.

verses.colloquial: tasya saptadhaa praanta bhuumih prajnaa .. .27..
verses.translation_reworded: His knowledge reaches the sevenfold highest ground.

verses.colloquial: yoga anga anushthaanaad ashuddhi kshaye jnaana diiptih aa viveka khyaateh .. .28..
verses.translation_reworded: As practice of the various parts of Yoga destroys impurities, knowledge grows radiant, up to discrimination.

verses.colloquial: yama niyama aasana praanaayaama pratyaahaara dhaaranaa dhyaana samaadhayo'shtaavangaani .. .29..
verses.translation_reworded: The eight limbs of Yoga are Yama, Niyama, Āsana, Prānāyāma, Pratyāhāra, Dhāranā, Dhyāna and Samādhi.

verses.colloquial: ahimsaa satya aasteya brahmacharyaa parigrahaa yamaah .. .30..
verses.translation_reworded: The Yamas are non-killing, truthfulness, non-stealing, continence and non-receiving.

verses.colloquial: jaati desha kaala samaya anavacchinnaah saarvabhaumaa mahaavratam .. .31..
verses.translation_reworded: When not limited by time, place, purpose or caste rules, these are the universal great vows.

verses.colloquial: shaucha samtosha tapah svaadhyaaya iishvara pranidhaanaani niyamaah .. .32..
verses.translation_reworded: The Niyamas are internal and external purification, contentment, mortification, study and worship of God.

verses.colloquial: vitarka baadhane pratipaksha bhaavanam .. .33..
verses.translation_reworded: To block thoughts hostile to Yoga, bring up opposing thoughts.

verses.sanskrit:
वितर्का हिंसादयः कृतकारितानुमोदिता लोभक्रोधमोहपूर्वका
मृदुमध्याधिमात्रा दुःखाज्ञानानन्तफला इति प्रतिपक्षभावनम् ॥ २.३४॥
verses.roman:
vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā
mṛdumadhyādhimātrā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam .. 2.34..
verses.colloquial:
vitarkaa himsaadayah krita kaarita anumoditaa lobha krodha moha puurvakaa
mridu madhya adhi maatraa duhkha ajnaana ananta phalaa iti pratipaksha bhaavanam .. .34..
verses.translation_reworded: Killing, falsehood and the like obstruct Yoga, whether done, caused or approved; whether from avarice, anger or ignorance; whether slight, middling or great. They end in infinite ignorance and misery. Reflecting so is the method of thinking the contrary.

verses.colloquial: ahimsaa pratishthaayaam tat sannidhau vaira tyaagah .. .35..
verses.translation_reworded: Once non-killing is established, all enmity in others ceases in his presence.

verses.colloquial: satya pratishthaayaam kriyaa phala aashrayatvam .. .36..
verses.translation_reworded: Established in truthfulness, the Yogi gains the power to obtain the fruits of work, for himself and others, without the works.

verses.colloquial: asteya pratishthaayaam sarva ratna upasthaanam .. .37..
verses.translation_reworded: Once non-stealing is established, all wealth comes to the Yogi.

verses.colloquial: brahmacharya pratishthaayaam viirya laabhah .. .38..
verses.translation_reworded: Once continence is established, energy is gained.

verses.colloquial: aparigraha sthairye janma kathamtaa sambodhah .. .39..
verses.translation_reworded: Fixed in non-receiving, he gains memory of past life.

verses.colloquial: shauchaat svaanga jugupsaa parair asamsargah .. .40..
verses.translation_reworded: Once internal and external cleanliness are established, disgust for one's own body arises, along with non-intercourse with others.

verses.colloquial: sattva shuddhi saumanasya ekaagrya indriya jaya aatma darshana yogyatvaani cha .. .41..
verses.translation_reworded: Purification of the Sattva also arises, as do cheerfulness of mind, concentration, mastery of the organs, and fitness to realise the Self.

verses.colloquial: samtoshaad anuttama sukha laabhah .. .42..
verses.translation_reworded: Contentment brings supreme happiness.

verses.colloquial: kaaya indriya siddhih ashuddhi kshayaat tapasah .. .43..
verses.translation_reworded: Mortification destroys impurity and so brings powers to the organs and body.

verses.colloquial: svaadhyaayaad ishta devataa samprayogah .. .44..
verses.translation_reworded: Repeating the Mantra brings realisation of the intended deity.

verses.colloquial: samaadhi siddhir iishvara pranidhaanaat .. .45..
verses.translation_reworded: Samadhi comes through sacrificing all to Ishvara.

verses.colloquial: sthira sukham aasanam .. .46..
verses.translation_reworded: Posture is what is firm and pleasant.

verses.colloquial: prayatna shaithilya ananta samaapatti bhyaam .. .47..
verses.translation_reworded: Posture becomes firm and pleasant by lessening the natural tendency to restlessness and meditating on the unlimited.

verses.colloquial: tato dvandvaan abhighaatah .. .48..
verses.translation_reworded: When the seat is mastered, dualities no longer obstruct.

verses.colloquial: tasmin sati shvaasa prashvaasayor gati vicchedah praanaayaamah .. .49..
verses.translation_reworded: After this comes control of the movement of exhalation and inhalation.

verses.colloquial:
baahya abhyantara stambha vrittih desha kaala samkhyaabhih
paridrishto diirgha suukshmah .. .50..
verses.translation_reworded: Its modifications are external, internal or motionless; they are regulated by place, time and number, and are long or short.

verses.colloquial: baahya abhyantara vishaya aakshepii chaturthah .. .51..
verses.translation_reworded: The fourth restrains the Prana through reflection on an external or internal object.

verses.colloquial: tatah kshiiyate prakaasha aavaranam .. .52..
verses.translation_reworded: From that, the covering over the light of the Chitta thins away.

verses.colloquial: dhaaranaasu cha yogyataa manasah .. .53..
verses.translation_reworded: The mind grows fit for Dharana.

verses.colloquial: svavishayaasamprayoge chitta svaruupa anukaara iva indriyaanaam pratyaahaarah .. .54..
verses.translation_reworded: The organs are drawn in when they leave their own objects and take on, as it were, the form of the mind-stuff.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः परमा वश्यतेन्द्रियाणाम् ॥ २.५५॥
॥ इति पतञ्जलि-विरचिते योग-सूत्रे द्वितीयः साधन-पादः ॥
verses.roman:
tataḥ paramā vaśyatendriyāṇām .. 2.55..
.. iti patañjali-viracite yoga-sūtre dvitīyaḥ sādhana-pādaḥ ..
verses.colloquial:
tatah paramaa vashya indriyaanaam ..
.. iti patanjali virachite yoga suutre dvitiiyah saadhana paadah ..
verses.translation_reworded: From that comes supreme mastery of the organs.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part 3 - Vibhūti-Pāda - Powers</vt>
देशबन्धश्चित्तस्य धारणा ॥ ३.१॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part 3 - Vibhūti-Pāda - Powers</vt>
deśabandhaścittasya dhāraṇā .. 3.1..
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part  - Vibhuuti-Paada - Powers</vt>
desha bandhash chittasya dhaaranaa .. .1..
verses.translation_reworded: Dhāranā is fixing the mind on a particular object.

verses.colloquial: tatra pratyaya ekataanataa dhyaanam .. .2..
verses.translation_reworded: Dhyāna is an unbroken flow of knowledge in that object.

verses.colloquial: tad eva artha maatra nirbhaasam svaruupa shuunyam iva samaadhih .. .3..
verses.translation_reworded: When that drops all forms and reflects the meaning alone, it is Samādhi.

verses.colloquial: trayam ekatra samyamah .. .4..
verses.translation_reworded: These three, practised on one object, are Samyama.

verses.colloquial: tajjayaat prajnaa lokah .. .5..
verses.translation_reworded: Mastery of that brings the light of knowledge.

verses.colloquial: tasya bhuumishu viniyogah .. .6..
verses.translation_reworded: It should be applied in stages.

verses.colloquial: trayam antarangam puurvebhyah .. .7..
verses.translation_reworded: These three are more internal than the preceding ones.

verses.colloquial: tad api bahir angam nirbiijasya .. .8..
verses.translation_reworded: Yet even they are external to seedless Samadhi.

verses.colloquial:
vyutthaana nirodha samskaarayoh abhibhava praadurbhaavau
nirodha kshana chitta anvayah nirodha parinaamah .. .9..
verses.translation_reworded: When the disturbed impressions of the mind are suppressed and impressions of control arise, the mind persisting in that moment of control is said to attain the controlling modifications.

verses.colloquial: tasya prashaanta vaahitaa samskaaraat .. .10..
verses.translation_reworded: Habit steadies its flow.

verses.colloquial: sarvaarthat aikaagratayoh kshayodayau chittasya samaadhi parinaamah .. .11..
verses.translation_reworded: When the power of taking in all sorts of objects is destroyed and the power of concentrating on one object is manifested, the Chitta gains the modification called Samadhi.

verses.colloquial: tatah punah shaanta uditau tulya pratyayau chittasya ekaagrataa parinaamah .. .12..
verses.translation_reworded: The Chitta is one-pointed when the past impression and the present one are alike.

verses.colloquial: etena bhuuta indriyeshu dharma lakshana avasthaa parinaamaa vyaakhyaataah .. .13..
verses.translation_reworded: This explains the threefold transformation of form, time and state, in fine or gross matter and in the organs.

verses.colloquial: shaanta udita avyapadeshya dharma anupaatii dharmii .. .14..
verses.translation_reworded: The qualified is what transformation acts upon, whether past, present or yet to be manifested.

verses.colloquial: kramaanyatvam parinaama anyatve hetuh .. .15..
verses.translation_reworded: The succession of changes causes manifold evolution.

verses.colloquial: parinaama traya samyamaad atiita anaagata jnaanam .. .16..
verses.translation_reworded: Samyama on the three kinds of change gives knowledge of past and future.

verses.colloquial:
shabda artha pratyayaanaam ita retara adhyaasaat
sankarah tat pravibhaaga samyamaat sarva bhuuta ruta jnaanam .. .17..
verses.translation_reworded: Word, meaning, and knowledge are ordinarily confused. Samyama on them gives knowledge of all animal sounds.

verses.colloquial: samskaara saakshaatkaranaat puurva jaatijnaanam .. .18..
verses.translation_reworded: Perceiving the impressions gives knowledge of past life.

verses.colloquial: pratyayasya para chitta jnaanam .. .19..
verses.translation_reworded: Samyama on the signs in another person's body gives knowledge of that person's mind.

verses.colloquial: na cha tat saalambanam tasya avishayiibhuutatvaat .. .20..
verses.translation_reworded: But not of the mind's contents, since those are not the object of the Samyama.

verses.colloquial:
kaaya ruupa samyamaat tadgraahya shakti stambhe
chakshuh prakaasha asamprayoge'ntardhaanam .. .21..
verses.translation_reworded: With Samyama on the form of the body, its perceptibility is blocked and the power of manifestation in the eye is cut off, so the Yogi's body becomes unseen.

verses.colloquial: etena shabda aadi antardhaanam uktam .. .22..
verses.translation_reworded: This also explains how spoken words and similar things can disappear or be concealed.

verses.sanskrit:
सोपक्रमं निरुपक्रमं च कर्म
तत्संयमादपरान्तज्ञानमरिष्टेभ्यो वा ॥
verses.roman:
sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca karma
tatsaṃyamādaparāntajñānamariṣṭebhyo vā .. 3.23..
verses.colloquial:
sopakramam nirupakramam cha karma
tat samyamaad aparaanta jnaanam arishtebhyo vaa .. .23..
verses.translation_reworded: Karma is of two kinds: soon to bear fruit and late to bear fruit. Through Samyama on these, or through the portents called Arishta, Yogis know the exact time they will leave their bodies.

verses.colloquial: maitry aadishu balaani .. .24..
verses.translation_reworded: Samyama on friendship, mercy, and the like (I.33) makes the Yogi excel in those qualities.

verses.colloquial: baleshu hasti balaadiini .. .25..
verses.translation_reworded: Samyama on the strength of the elephant and other creatures brings their strength to the Yogi.

verses.colloquial: pravritti aaloka nyaasa aat suukshma vyavahita viprakrishta jnaanam .. .26..
verses.translation_reworded: Samyama on the Effulgent Light (I.36) gives knowledge of what is fine, obstructed, and remote.

verses.colloquial: bhuvana jnaanam suurye samyamaat .. .27..
verses.translation_reworded: Samyama on the sun gives knowledge of the world.

verses.colloquial: chandre taaraa vyuuha jnaanam .. .28..
verses.translation_reworded: On the moon: knowledge of the clusters of stars.

verses.colloquial: dhruve tadgati jnaanam .. .29..
verses.translation_reworded: On the pole-star: knowledge of the movements of the stars.

verses.colloquial: naabhi chakre kaaya vyuuha jnaanam .. .30..
verses.translation_reworded: On the navel circle: knowledge of how the body is constituted.

verses.colloquial: kantha kuupe kshut pipaasaa nivrittih .. .31..
verses.translation_reworded: On the hollow of the throat: hunger ceases.

verses.colloquial: kuurma naadyaam sthairyam .. .32..
verses.translation_reworded: On the nerve called Kurma: the body becomes fixed.

verses.colloquial: muurdha jyotishi siddha darshanam .. .33..
verses.translation_reworded: On the light coming from the top of the head: sight of the Siddhas.

verses.colloquial: praatibhaad vaa sarvam .. .34..
verses.translation_reworded: Or all knowledge, through the power of Prātibha.

verses.colloquial: hridaye chitta samvit .. .35..
verses.translation_reworded: In the heart: knowledge of minds.

verses.roman:
sattva puruṣayoratyanta asaṃkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ
parārthatvātsvārthasaṃyamātpuruṣajñānam .. 3.36..
verses.colloquial:
sattva purushayoh atyanta asamkiirnayoh pratyaya avishesho bhogah
paraarthatvaat svaartha samyamaat purusha jnaanam .. .36..
verses.translation_reworded: Enjoyment arises from failing to distinguish the soul from Sattva, which are wholly different, since Sattva acts for another. Samyama on the self-centred one gives knowledge of the Purusha.

verses.colloquial: tatah praatibha shraavana vedana aadarsha aasvaada vaartaa jaayante .. .37..
verses.translation_reworded: From that arise the knowledge belonging to Pratibha and supernatural hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell.

verses.colloquial: te samaadhau upasargaa vyutthaane siddhayah .. .38..
verses.translation_reworded: These obstruct Samadhi, but in the worldly state they are powers.

verses.colloquial:
bandha kaarana shaithilyaat prachaara samvedanaaccha
chittasya para shariira aaveshah .. .39..
verses.translation_reworded: When the cause of the Chitta's bondage has loosened, the Yogi, knowing its channels of activity (the nerves), enters another's body.

verses.colloquial: udaana jayaaj jala panka kantaka aadishu asanga utkraantish cha .. .40..
verses.translation_reworded: Conquering the current called Udāna, the Yogi does not sink in water or swamps, can walk on thorns and the like, and can die at will.

verses.colloquial: samaana jayaat jvalanam .. .41..
verses.translation_reworded: Conquering the current Samāna, he is surrounded by a blaze of light.

verses.colloquial: shrotra aakaashayoh sambandha samyamaad divyam shrotram .. .42..
verses.translation_reworded: Samyama on the relation between the ear and the Akasha gives divine hearing.

verses.colloquial:
kaaya aakaashayoh sambandha samyamaat laghu tuula-
samaapattes cha aakaasha gamanam .. .43..
verses.translation_reworded: Through Samyama on the relation between the Akasha and the body, and by becoming as light as cotton-wool and the like through meditating on them, the Yogi travels through the skies.

verses.colloquial: bahir akalpitaa vrittir mahaavidehaa tatah prakaasha aavarana kshayah .. .44..
verses.translation_reworded: Samyama on the "real modifications" of the mind outside the body, called great disembodiedness, removes the covering over light.

verses.colloquial: sthuula svaruupa suukshma anvaya artha vattva samyamaad bhuuta jayah .. .45..
verses.translation_reworded: Mastery of the elements comes from Samyama on their gross and fine forms, their essential traits, the Gunas inherent in them, and their contribution to the soul's experience.

verses.colloquial: tato 'nimaadi praadurbhaavah kaaya sampat tad dharmaan abhighaatash cha .. .46..
verses.translation_reworded: From that come minuteness and the other powers, the "glorification of the body," and the indestructibility of the body's qualities.

verses.colloquial: ruupa laavanya balavajra samhanana tvaani kaaya sampat .. .47..
verses.translation_reworded: The "glorification of the body" means beauty, complexion, strength, and adamantine hardness.

verses.colloquial: grahana svaruupa asmitaa anvaya artha vattva samyamaad indriya jayah .. .48..
verses.translation_reworded: Conquest of the organs comes from Samyama on their objectivity and power of illumination, on egoism, on the Gunas inherent in them, and on their contribution to the soul's experience.

verses.colloquial: tato manojavitvam vikarana bhaavah pradhaana jayash cha .. .49..
verses.translation_reworded: From that the body gains rapid movement like the mind's, the organs gain power independent of the body, and nature is conquered.

verses.colloquial:
sattva purusha anyataa khyaati maatrasya sarva bhaava adhishthaatritvam
sarva jnaatritvam cha .. .50..
verses.translation_reworded: Samyama on the discrimination between Sattva and Purusha brings omnipotence and omniscience.

verses.colloquial: tad vairaagyaad api dosha biija kshaye kaivalyam .. .51..
verses.translation_reworded: Giving up even these powers destroys the very seed of evil, which leads to Kaivalya.

verses.colloquial: sthaani upanimantrane sanga smaya aakaranam punah anishta prasangaat .. .52..
verses.translation_reworded: The Yogi should not be tempted or flattered by the advances of celestial beings, for fear of evil returning.

verses.colloquial: kshana tat kramayoh samyamaad vivekajam jnaanam .. .53..
verses.translation_reworded: Samyama on a particle of time and on what precedes and follows it brings discrimination.

verses.colloquial: jaati lakshana deshair anyataa navacchedaat tulyayoh tatah pratipattih .. .54..
verses.translation_reworded: Even things that cannot be told apart by species, sign, or place are distinguished by this Samyama.

verses.sanskrit:
तारकं सर्वविषयं सर्वथाविषयम् अक्रमं
चेति विवेकजं ज्ञानम् ॥
verses.roman:
tārakaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ sarvathāviṣayam akramaṃ
ceti vivekajaṃ jñānam .. 3.55..
verses.colloquial:
taarakam sarva vishayam sarvathaa vishayam akramam
cheti vivekajam jnaanam .. .55..
verses.translation_reworded: The saving knowledge is that knowledge of discrimination which covers all objects, in all their variations, at once.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्त्वपुरुषयोः शुद्धिसाम्ये कैवल्यमिति ॥
॥ इति पतञ्जलि-विरचिते योग-सूत्रे तृतीयो विभूति-पादः ॥
verses.roman:
sattvapuruṣayoḥ śuddhisāmye kaivalyamiti .. 3.56..
.. iti patañjali-viracite yoga-sūtre tṛtīyo vibhūti-pādaḥ ..
verses.colloquial:
sattva purushayoh shuddhi saamye kaivalyam iti ..
.. iti patanjali-virachite yoga-suutre tritiiyo vibhuuti-paadah ..
verses.translation_reworded: When Sattva and Purusha are alike in purity, Kaivalya comes.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part 4 - Kaivalya-pāda - Liberation</vt>
जन्मौषधिमन्त्रतपःसमाधिजाः सिद्धयः ॥ ४.१॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part 4 - Kaivalya-pāda - Liberation</vt>
janmauṣadhimantratapaḥsamādhijāḥ siddhayaḥ .. 4.1..
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Patanjali Yogasutra: Part  - Kaivalya-paada - Liberation</vt>
janma aushadhi mantra tapah samaadhi jaah siddhayah .. .1..
verses.translation_reworded: Birth, chemical means, the power of words, mortification, or concentration can each bring the Siddhis (powers).

verses.colloquial: jaati antara parinaamah prakrityaa puuraat .. .2..
verses.translation_reworded: Change into another species comes through the filling in of nature.

verses.colloquial:
nimittam aprayojakam prakritiinaam varana bhedas tu
tatah kshetrika vat .. .3..
verses.translation_reworded: Good and bad deeds do not directly cause the transformations of nature. They break the obstacles to its evolution, as a farmer breaks the barriers to water, which then flows down by its own nature.

verses.colloquial: nirmaana chittaani asmitaa maatraat .. .4..
verses.translation_reworded: The created minds arise from egoism alone.

verses.colloquial: pravritti bhede prayojakam chittam ekam anekeshaam .. .5..
verses.translation_reworded: Though the created minds act in various ways, the one original mind controls them all.

verses.colloquial: tatra dhyaana jam anaashayam .. .6..
verses.translation_reworded: Among the various Chittas, the one attained by Samadhi is free of desire.

verses.colloquial: karmaashuklaakrishnam yoginas trividham itareshaam .. .7..
verses.translation_reworded: For Yogis, works are neither black nor white. For others they are of three kinds: black, white, and mixed.

verses.colloquial: tatas tad vipaaka anugunaanaam eva abhivyaktih vaasanaanaam .. .8..
verses.translation_reworded: From these three kinds of work, each state manifests only the desires that suit that state. (The others are held in abeyance for the time being.)

verses.colloquial:
jaati desha kaala vyavahitaanaam apy aanantaryam
smriti samskaarayoh eka ruupatvaat .. .9..
verses.translation_reworded: Desires follow in sequence even when separated by species, space, and time, because memory and impressions are identical.

verses.colloquial: taasaam anaaditvam cha aashisho nityatvaat .. .10..
verses.translation_reworded: Since the thirst for happiness is eternal, desires have no beginning.

verses.colloquial: hetu phala aashraya aalambanaih samgrihiita tvaat eshaam abhaave tad abhaavah .. .11..
verses.translation_reworded: Desires are held together by cause, effect, support, and objects. Without these, they cease.

verses.colloquial: atiita anaagatam svaruupatah asti adhva bhedaat dharmaanaam .. .12..
verses.translation_reworded: Past and future exist in their own nature, since qualities take different paths.

verses.colloquial: te vyakta suukshmaa guna aatmaanah .. .13..
verses.translation_reworded: They are either manifest or fine, being of the nature of the Gunas.

verses.colloquial: parinaama ekatvaad vastu tattvam .. .14..
verses.translation_reworded: Things are unified because their changes are unified.

verses.colloquial: vastu saamye chitta bhedaat tayor vibhaktah panthaah .. .15..
verses.translation_reworded: Since perception and desire differ with regard to the same object, mind and object differ in nature.

verses.sanskrit: न चैकचित्ततन्त्रं वस्तु तदप्रमाणकं तदा किं स्यात् ॥ ४.१६॥
verses.roman: na caikacittatantraṃ vastu tadapramāṇakaṃ tadā kiṃ syāt .. 4.16..
verses.colloquial: na cha eka chitta tantram vastu tad apramaanakam tadaa kim syaat .. .16..
verses.translation_reworded: An object cannot be said to depend on the perception of a single mind. If it did, it could be called non-existent whenever that mind was not perceiving it.

verses.colloquial: tad uparaaga apekshitvaac chittasya vastu jnaata ajnaatam .. .17..
verses.translation_reworded: Things are known or unknown to the mind according to the colouring they give it.

verses.colloquial: sadaa jnaataash chitta vrittayas tat prabhoh purushasya aparinaamitvaat .. .18..
verses.translation_reworded: The states of the mind are always known, since the mind's lord, the Purusha, does not change.

verses.colloquial: na tat svaabhaasam drishyatvaat .. .19..
verses.translation_reworded: The mind is not self-luminous, since it is an object.

verses.colloquial: eka samaye cha ubhaya anavadhaaranam .. .20..
verses.translation_reworded: Because it cannot perceive both at once.

verses.colloquial: chitta antara drishye buddhi buddher ati prasangah smriti sankarash cha .. .21..
verses.translation_reworded: If a further perceiving mind is assumed, such assumptions never end, and memory falls into confusion.

verses.colloquial: chiter apratisamkramaayaas tad aakaaraapattau svabuddhi samvedanam .. .22..
verses.translation_reworded: The essence of knowledge (the Purusha) never changes; the mind becomes conscious when it takes on that form.

verses.colloquial: drashtri drishya uparaktam chittam sarva artham .. .23..
verses.translation_reworded: Tinged by both seer and seen, the mind can understand everything.

verses.colloquial: tad asamkhyeya vaasanaabhish chitram api paraartham samhatya kaaritvaat .. .24..
verses.translation_reworded: Though patterned by countless desires, the mind works for another (the Purusha), since it works in combination.

verses.colloquial: visheshadarshina aatmabhaava bhaavanaa vinivrittih .. .25..
verses.translation_reworded: For one who discriminates, seeing the mind as Atman comes to an end.

verses.colloquial: tadaa viveka nimnam kaivalya praagbhaaram chittam .. .26..
verses.translation_reworded: Then the mind, intent on discrimination, reaches the prior state of Kaivalya (isolation).

verses.colloquial: tac chidreshu pratyaya antaraani samskaarebhyah .. .27..
verses.translation_reworded: Thoughts that arise to obstruct this come from impressions.

verses.colloquial: haanam eshaam kleshavad uktam .. .28..
verses.translation_reworded: They are destroyed in the same way as ignorance, egoism, and the rest, as stated earlier (II.10).

verses.colloquial:
prasamkhyaane'py akusiidasya sarvathaa
vivekakhyaater dharma meghah samaadhih .. .29..
verses.translation_reworded: One who gives up the fruits even on reaching right discriminating knowledge of the essences gains, through perfect discrimination, the Samadhi called the cloud of virtue.

verses.colloquial: tatah klesha karma nivrittih .. .30..
verses.translation_reworded: From that, pain and works cease.

verses.colloquial: tadaa sarva aavarana mala apetasya jnaanasya aanantyaat jneyam alpam .. .31..
verses.translation_reworded: When knowledge, stripped of coverings and impurities, becomes infinite, what can be known becomes small.

verses.colloquial: tatah kritaarthaanaam parinaama krama samaaptih gunaanaam .. .32..
verses.translation_reworded: Then the successive transformations of the qualities end, their goal being reached.

verses.colloquial: kshana pratiyogii parinaama aparaanta nirgraahyah kramah .. .33..
verses.translation_reworded: Succession is the changes that relate to moments and are perceived at the far end of a series.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरुषार्थशून्यानां गुणानां प्रतिप्रसवः कैवल्यं
स्वरूपप्रतिष्ठा वा चितिशक्तिरिति ॥ ४.३४॥
*****
॥ इति पतञ्जलि-विरचिते योग-सूत्रे चतुर्थः कैवल्य-पादः ॥
॥ इति श्री पातञ्जल-योग-सूत्राणि ॥
verses.roman:
puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ
svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktiriti .. 4.34..
*****
.. iti patañjali-viracite yoga-sūtre caturthaḥ kaivalya-pādaḥ ..
.. iti śrī pātañjala-yoga-sūtrāṇi ..
verses.colloquial:
purushaartha shuunyaanaam gunaanaam prati prasavah kaivalyam
svaruupa pratishthaa vaa chiti shaktih iti ..
*****
.. iti patanjali virachite yoga suutre chaturthah kaivalya paadah ..
.. iti shrii paatanjala yoga suutraani ..
verses.translation_reworded: Kaivalya is the qualities resolving in reverse order, with no motive of action left for the Purusha; or it is the power of knowledge established in its own nature.
